content:
You can left-align table captions by redefining `\@makecaption` (which is what the `caption` package normally does for you). Here is a minimal way to do it **without any extra packages**.

### 1. Left-align all captions globally

Put this in your preamble:

```latex
\makeatletter
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \noindent #1: #2\par
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatother
```

Now all figure and table captions will be left-aligned.

---

### 2. Left-align only specific captions (local change)

If you only want certain tables to have left-aligned captions, you can do:

```latex
\begingroup
\makeatletter
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \noindent #1: #2\par
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatother

\begin{table}[h]
  \centering
  \begin{tabular}{ll}
    a & b \\
  \end{tabular}
  \caption{This caption is left-aligned}
\end{table}

\endgroup
```

The redefinition is confined to the group (`\begingroup` ... `\endgroup`), so other captions keep their original formatting.

---

### 3. If you only care about the **text** being ragged-right

If you don’t mind the label placement but just want non-centered text, you can also do:

```latex
\caption[Short title]{\raggedright Long explanation of the table caption.\par}
```

but depending on your class, the overall caption box may still be centered; the `\@makecaption` redefinition is the robust solution.
